events.message:
bip-0327: add test vectors and describe their purpose

Add Sign test vectors for a secnonce with k2' = 0 and for a secnonce
generated for a different public key. No previous test vector detected
an implementation that checks only k1', or one that omits the public
key check added in 1.0.0-rc.2.

Add test vectors for a single signer, a 4-byte extra_in, and plain and
x-only tweaks in DeterministicSign. They detect implementations that
reject a single signer, encode the length of extra_in as a constant,
or treat every tweak in DeterministicSign as x-only.

State in the BIP that each test vector should detect a plausible
implementation mistake that no other test vector detects, and that all
inputs in the test vectors have the lengths that the algorithms
require.

Give each added test vector a rationale field that names the mistake it
detects. The field is separate from the comment field because some
implementations derive the expected error from the comment.

Co-authored-by: Ferdinando Ametrano <ferdinando@ametrano.net>

bip-0327: add test vectors for k2' >= n and 256-byte messages

Add Sign test vectors with k2' = n and k2' = n + 1. Together they
detect implementations that check the secret nonce values only for
zero, that check k2' <= n instead of k2' < n, or that reduce k2' mod n
before checking it for zero. No single value detects the last two:
among values of at least n, checking k2' <= n accepts only n, while
reducing first rejects only n. For k2' = n, the optional correctness
check at the end of Sign also fails, because k2'*G is infinity, so this
vector detects the k2' <= n mistake only in implementations that omit
that check.

Add NonceGen and DeterministicSign test vectors with a 256-byte
message. They detect implementations that encode only the low byte of
len(m); the longest message in the previous test vectors has 38 bytes.
DeterministicSign needs its own vector because it encodes len(m)
separately.

bip-0327: add test vectors for a public key and its negation

A public key and its negation have the same X coordinate, and their
compressed encodings differ only in the first byte. Add a Sign test
vector with a secnonce generated for the negation of the signer's public
key, and a KeyAgg test vector with a public key and its negation. They
detect implementations that compare public keys only by their X
coordinates, in the public key check of Sign, in GetSecondKey, or in
KeyAggCoeffInternal. Distinct public keys in the previous test vectors
also have distinct X coordinates.

The public key check in Sign ensures that the secret key provided to
Sign is determined when NonceGen is invoked. Comparing only X
coordinates determines the secret key only up to negation.

bip-0327: add a NonceGen test vector without repeated bytes

In the previous NonceGen test vectors, every rand_ consists of the byte
0F repeated 32 times, every present sk of the byte 02 repeated 32 times,
and every pk has an even Y coordinate. Add a test vector whose rand_ and
sk are not a repeated byte and whose pk has an odd Y coordinate. It
detects implementations that reverse the byte order of rand_ or sk, that
replace the first byte of pk with 02, or that use only the first byte of
rand_.

With the last mistake, two NonceGen invocations with the same other
arguments return the same secnonce with probability 1/256, although the
BIP requires that Sign is never executed twice with the same secnonce.

bip-0327: isolate the range check in a PartialSigVerify test vector

The PartialSigVerify test vector with the partial signature n fails the
verification equation even without the range check. So it does not
detect implementations that omit the range check or that check s > n
instead of s >= n. Change the pubnonces of the test vector such that the
partial signature 0 is valid, keeping the aggregate nonce. Since
n*G = 0*G, the partial signature n then satisfies the verification
equation, and only the range check rejects it. The previous version of
the test vector detects no mistake that the new version does not detect,
so it is replaced rather than kept.

gen_vectors_helper.py computes the new pubnonces.

bip-0327: add test vectors for the signs of accumulated tweaks

ApplyTweak multiplies gacc by g, which is -1 if an x-only tweak negates
the aggregate public key. In every previous tweak sequence, the product
of all values of g equals the last one. Add a test vector with two
x-only tweaks, of which only the first negates the aggregate public key.
It detects implementations that set gacc to g instead of multiplying it
by g.

PartialSigAgg adds e*g*tacc, where g is -1 if the aggregate public key Q
has an odd Y coordinate. In the previous PartialSigAgg test vectors,
tacc is 0 whenever Q has an odd Y coordinate. Add a test vector with a
plain tweak and an odd Q, generated by gen_vectors_helper.py. It detects
implementations that omit g.

bip-0327: bump version to 1.0.5

Add a changelog entry for the changes to the test vectors.

events.body: Ideally, we try those test vectors in an implementation (libsecp? btclib-ecc? ...) before a merge.

tACK 2061baf3

You asked for these vectors to be tried in an implementation, and #2329 came from btclib-org/ecc's tests, so I ran them there. ecc passes every case of the six changed files: 359 passed, 4 skipped, the same four tests that skip with the 1.0.4 vectors, and every case runs in ecc's own vector tests. The reference implementation's tests pass too. I also made each mistake a rationale names in `reference.py`, one at a time: each such copy passes the 1.0.4 vectors and fails these, with one exception.

The exception is the 4-byte `extra_in` case, whose rationale should read "Detects implementations that encode the length of extra_in as 32 whenever extra_in is present". The constant 32 it names now is already caught by the NonceGen vector with every optional argument absent.

Details: https://gist.github.com/fametrano/b4bd8510da2f247f27d324b2d7e25623/7e4ef292a5e559b8b74d7f2cf66afa799c6d7398

Concept ACK 2061baf3313a69f35eebca714389f03dc817fd07

I ran `reference.py` and `gen_vectors_helper.py` at this commit: the tests pass, and the generated sig_agg vectors match the JSON.


 I also applied the mistakes that the rationales of the new `Sign` error vectors name to `reference.py`, one at a time, and recorded which vectors detect each mistake. Every new vector detects the mistake its rationale names, but two rationales name a mistake that another new vector also detects (see inline), as does the rationale of the 4-byte `extra_in` vector that fametrano pointed out. I think this is fine for test vectors, but it contradicts the new requirement that each test vector detect a mistake that no other test vector detects, so I suggest dropping that requirement (see inline).

(Reviewed with the help of Claude Opus 5.5)

 Standalone JSON test vectors are also available in the [[bip-0327|same directory]], to facilitate porting the test vectors into other implementations.
 
+Each test vector should detect a plausible implementation mistake that no other test vector detects.
comments.body:
I suggest dropping this requirement. The existing test vectors probably do not meet it, and three of the new ones do not either: the 4-byte `extra_in` vector (see fametrano's review) and two `Sign` error vectors (see my other comments). Checking it requires comparing each vector against all others, which makes it hard to maintain whenever a vector is added. A rationale that names a mistake the vector detects is useful without it.

```suggestion
```

comments.body:
The vectors with k2' = n and k2' > n also detect this mistake: an implementation that checks only k1' signs both without an error. The mistake that only this vector detects is a missing check that k2' is nonzero. If the requirement that each test vector detect a mistake that no other test vector detects stays, the rationale should name that one.

```suggestion
            "rationale": "Detects implementations that check only that k2' < n"
```

comments.body:
The vector with the negated public key below also detects this mistake. The mistakes that only this vector detects are using secnonce[64:97] as the signer's public key, and checking only that secnonce[64:97] is one of the public keys: this secnonce's public key belongs to the second signer, while the negated key in the other vector belongs to no signer. If the requirement that each test vector detect a mistake that no other test vector detects stays, the rationale should name those.

```suggestion
            "rationale": "Detects implementations that check only that secnonce[64:97] is one of the public keys, or that use secnonce[64:97] instead of the public key of sk"
```
